answer: The SAR backscatter analysis identifies a flooded region with 266 water pixels, representing 0.41% of the total area, based on a VV polarization threshold of -16.0 dB. This SAR-derived water mask shows low agreement with the optical water mask (IoU = 0.011), indicating minimal overlap between the two detection methods. The optical mask highlights 10,770 pixels as water, covering 16.4% of the scene, but only 123 pixels are common to both masks. The SAR water detection is calibrated and processed using a 3x3 boxcar filter and morphological opening, with SDWI statistics (mean = -11.72) not used for the final mask. The flooded region appears as a dark, coherent patch in the lower right quadrant, consistent with the SAR water threshold.
